subproblems.title: C¹ compactly supported radial potential with gradient g(|y|²)·y
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let r > 0, and let g : ℝ → ℝ be continuous with g(t) = 0 for every t ≥ r². Then there is Ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) such that (a) Ψ is C¹ on ℝⁿ, (b) Ψ has compact support, (c) tsupport Ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, r), and (d) DΨ(y)v = g(|y|²)·⟨y, v⟩ for all y, v ∈ ℝⁿ, where DΨ(y) = fderiv ℝ Ψ y and ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < r → Continuous g → (∀ t : ℝ, r ^ 2 ≤ t → g t = 0) → ∃ Ψ : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 Ψ ∧ HasCompactSupport Ψ ∧ tsupport Ψ ⊆ closedBall 0 r ∧ ∀ y v : Euclid n, fderiv ℝ Ψ y v = g (‖y‖ ^ 2) * inner ℝ y v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof, the radial potential Ψ(y) = P(|y|²) with P(t) = ½∫_{r²}^t g, with every detail supplied.

Notation: ℝⁿ = Euclid n; |·| and ⟨·,·⟩ are the Euclidean norm and inner product; DF(y) = fderiv ℝ F y.

1. (The profile P.) Define P : ℝ → ℝ by P(t) := ½·∫_{r²}^{t} g(τ) dτ (oriented interval integral). Since g is continuous, the fundamental theorem of calculus (Continuous.integral_hasStrictDerivAt) shows that t ↦ ∫_{r²}^{t} g has derivative g(t) at every t ∈ ℝ. Hence P has derivative P'(t) = ½·g(t) at every t ∈ ℝ.

2. (P is C¹.) P is differentiable everywhere and P' = ½·g is continuous, so P is C¹ (contDiff_one_iff_deriv).

3. (P vanishes beyond r².) Let t ≥ r². Every τ between r² and t satisfies τ ≥ r², so g(τ) = 0. Hence ∫_{r²}^{t} g = ∫_{r²}^{t} 0 = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr on uIcc r² t = [r², t]), and P(t) = 0.

4. (Definition of Ψ; property (a).) Put N(y) := |y|² and Ψ := P ∘ N, i.e. Ψ(y) = P(|y|²). N is C^∞ on ℝⁿ (contDiff_norm_sq) and P is C¹ by step 2, so Ψ is C¹ (ContDiff.comp). This is (a).

5. (Derivative; property (d).) N is differentiable at every y with DN(y)v = 2⟨y, v⟩ (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq: DN(y) = 2 • innerSL ℝ y). By the chain rule (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt), Ψ is differentiable at y and DΨ(y) = P'(|y|²)·DN(y). Hence DΨ(y)v = ½·g(|y|²)·2⟨y, v⟩ = g(|y|²)·⟨y, v⟩ for all y, v. This is (d).

6. (Support; property (c).) Let |y| ≥ r. Since r > 0, |y|² ≥ r² (pow_le_pow_left₀), so Ψ(y) = P(|y|²) = 0 by step 3. Hence every y with Ψ(y) ≠ 0 satisfies |y| < r, so support Ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, r). As closedBall(0, r) is closed, tsupport Ψ = closure(support Ψ) ⊆ closedBall(0, r) (closure_minimal). This is (c).

7. (Compact support; property (b).) ℝⁿ is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence proper, so closedBall(0, r) is compact (isCompact_closedBall). tsupport Ψ is a closed subset of it by step 6, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). So Ψ has compact support. This is (b). ∎

  intro n r g hr hg hgr
  set P : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => (1/2 : ℝ) * ∫ τ in r ^ 2..t, g τ with hP
  have hPd : ∀ t, HasDerivAt P ((1/2 : ℝ) * g t) t := fun t =>
    ((hg.integral_hasStrictDerivAt (r ^ 2) t).hasDerivAt).const_mul (1/2 : ℝ)
  have hPC : ContDiff ℝ 1 P := by
    rw [contDiff_one_iff_deriv]
    refine ⟨fun t => (hPd t).differentiableAt, ?_⟩
    have : deriv P = fun t => (1/2 : ℝ) * g t := funext fun t => (hPd t).deriv
    rw [this]; exact continuous_const.mul hg
  have hP0 : ∀ t, r ^ 2 ≤ t → P t = 0 := by
    intro t ht
    simp only [hP]
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_congr (g := fun _ => (0:ℝ)) ?_]
    · simp
    · intro τ hτ
      rw [uIcc_of_le ht] at hτ
      exact hgr τ hτ.1
  have hsupp : tsupport (fun y : Euclid n => P (‖y‖ ^ 2)) ⊆ closedBall 0 r := by
    refine closure_minimal (fun y hy => ?_) isClosed_closedBall
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right]
    by_contra hlt
    push Not at hlt
    exact hy (hP0 _ (pow_le_pow_left₀ hr.le hlt.le 2))
  refine ⟨fun y => P (‖y‖ ^ 2), hPC.comp (contDiff_norm_sq ℝ), ?_, hsupp, ?_⟩
  · exact IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset (isCompact_closedBall 0 r) (isClosed_tsupport _) hsupp
  · intro y v
    have hd : HasFDerivAt (fun y : Euclid n => P (‖y‖ ^ 2))
        (((1/2 : ℝ) * g (‖y‖ ^ 2)) • (2 • innerSL ℝ y)) y :=
      (hPd _).comp_hasFDerivAt y (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq y).hasFDerivAt
    rw [hd.fderiv]
    simp only [smul_apply, innerSL_apply_apply, smul_eq_mul, nsmul_eq_mul]
    ring
proof_key_steps: P(t) := ½∫_{r²}^t g has P' = g/2 everywhere by the FTC, so P is C¹; P(t) = 0 for t ≥ r² because g vanishes on [r², t].
Ψ := P(|·|²) is C¹ as the composition of P with the smooth map y ↦ |y|².
The chain rule with D|y|² = 2⟨y, ·⟩ gives DΨ(y)v = g(|y|²)⟨y, v⟩.
Ψ(y) = 0 for |y| ≥ r, so tsupport Ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, r), which is compact; hence Ψ has compact support.

subproblems.title: Green's first identity for a compactly supported C¹ function against a C² function
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝⁿ (= Euclid n) be open, let G : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C² on V, and let Ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C¹ on ℝⁿ with compact support and tsupport Ψ ⊆ V. Write e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, DF(y) = fderiv ℝ F y and D²G(y)(a, b) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y ![a, b]; these are Mathlib's total functions, and their values off V are irrelevant. Then ∫_{ℝⁿ} Σ_{i<n} DΨ(y)e_i · DG(y)e_i dy = −∫_{ℝⁿ} Ψ(y)·Σ_{i<n} D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid n)) (G Ψ : Euclid n → ℝ), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 G V → ContDiff ℝ 1 Ψ → HasCompactSupport Ψ → tsupport Ψ ⊆ V → ∫ y : Euclid n, ∑ i : Fin n, fderiv ℝ Ψ y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) * fderiv ℝ G y (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = -∫ y : Euclid n, Ψ y * ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, bullets 3–6: integration by parts against Ψ in each coordinate direction e_i, then summation over i. Here it is stated for a general open V ⊇ tsupport Ψ.

The parent localised ∂_iG by a cutoff χ in order to apply a global integration-by-parts theorem. The pinned Mathlib theorem integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable only asks each factor to be differentiable on the topological support of the other, so the cutoff is unnecessary. Otherwise the argument is the parent's.

Notation: K := tsupport Ψ, which is compact with K ⊆ V. For y ∈ ℝⁿ, DG(y) = fderiv ℝ G y and D(DG)(y) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ G) y.

1. (Regularity of G on V.) V is open and G is C² on V, so DG is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen). Consequently:
- DG is continuous on V;
- DG is differentiable at every y ∈ V, since V is a neighbourhood of y;
- D(DG) is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
For every y and all a, b, D²G(y)(a, b) = D(DG)(y)(a)(b) (iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, valid for all y).

2. (Ψ off K.) If y ∉ K, Ψ vanishes on the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ∖K of y, so Ψ(y) = 0 and DΨ(y) = 0 (support_fderiv_subset). Since Ψ is C¹, Ψ and DΨ are continuous on ℝⁿ and Ψ is differentiable everywhere.

3. (Gluing and integrability criterion.) Let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous on V with f(y) = 0 for all y ∉ K.
- f is continuous on ℝⁿ. At y ∈ V this holds because V is an open neighbourhood of y. At y ∉ V we have y ∉ K (as K ⊆ V), and f ≡ 0 on the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ∖K of y.
- support f ⊆ K and K is closed, so tsupport f ⊆ K is compact.
- A continuous, compactly supported function is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport), so f is integrable.

4. (One direction.) Fix i, and put v := e_i and g_i(y) := DG(y)v. Let ev_v : (ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ) → ℝ, L ↦ L v; it is continuous linear, and g_i = ev_v ∘ DG.
- For y ∈ V, step 1 and the chain rule show that g_i is differentiable at y with Dg_i(y)w = D(DG)(y)(w)(v).
- In particular Dg_i(y)v = D(DG)(y)(v)(v) = D²G(y)(v, v).
- g_i and y ↦ Dg_i(y)v = D(DG)(y)(v)(v) are continuous on V.

5. (Integration by parts.) Apply integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/LineDeriv/IntegrationByParts.lean) with f := Ψ, g := g_i, direction v and Lebesgue measure. Its hypotheses hold:
- y ↦ DΨ(y)v·g_i(y), y ↦ Ψ(y)·Dg_i(y)v and y ↦ Ψ(y)g_i(y) are continuous on V (steps 2 and 4) and vanish off K (step 2), so they are integrable by step 3;
- Ψ is differentiable at every point, in particular on tsupport g_i;
- g_i is differentiable at every point of tsupport Ψ = K ⊆ V (step 4).
The theorem yields ∫ Ψ(y)·Dg_i(y)v dy = −∫ DΨ(y)v·g_i(y) dy.

6. (Identify the left side.) For every y, Ψ(y)·Dg_i(y)v = Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i). If y ∈ K ⊆ V this is step 4. If y ∉ K, both sides vanish because Ψ(y) = 0. Hence, for each i,
∫ Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy = −∫ DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i dy.   (∗)

7. (Sum over i.) For each i, the functions y ↦ DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i and y ↦ Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) = Ψ(y)·D(DG)(y)(e_i)(e_i) are continuous on V and vanish off K, so both are integrable by step 3. The integral of a finite sum of integrable functions is the sum of the integrals (integral_finsetSum). Using Ψ(y)·Σ_i c_i = Σ_i Ψ(y)c_i and (∗):
∫ Σ_i DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i dy
= Σ_i ∫ DΨ e_i·DG e_i
= Σ_i (−∫ Ψ·D²G(e_i, e_i))
= −∫ Σ_i Ψ(y)·D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy
= −∫ Ψ(y)·Σ_i D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy. ∎

subproblems.title: First and second derivatives of z ↦ h(x − s z) for an arbitrary h
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let h : ℝⁿ → ℝ (= Euclid n → ℝ) be an arbitrary function (no regularity assumed), let x ∈ ℝⁿ and s ∈ ℝ, and put G(z) := h(x − s z). Then for all y, a, b ∈ ℝⁿ: DG(y)a = −(s·Dh(x − s y)a) and D²G(y)(a, b) = s²·D²h(x − s y)(a, b). Here D = fderiv ℝ and D²F(y)(a, b) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 F y ![a, b] are Mathlib's total derivatives, which are 0 at points of non-differentiability.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (x : Euclid n) (s : ℝ) (y a b : Euclid n), fderiv ℝ (fun z : Euclid n => h (x - s • z)) y a = -(s * fderiv ℝ h (x - s • y) a) ∧ iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (fun z : Euclid n => h (x - s • z)) y ![a, b] = s ^ 2 * iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h (x - s • y) ![a, b]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4, first bullet, of the parent proof: DG(y) = −s·Dh(x − s y) and D²G(y)(a, b) = s²·D²h(x − s y)(a, b). Here it is proved for an arbitrary function h and every y. The identities hold even where h is not differentiable, because z ↦ x − s z is an affine isomorphism when s ≠ 0 and constant when s = 0.

1. (Case s = 0.) Then G(z) = h(x) for all z, so G is constant. Hence DG(y) = 0, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G y = 0 (iteratedFDeriv_const_of_ne, since 2 ≠ 0). The right-hand sides are −(0·Dh(x)a) = 0 and 0²·D²h(x)(a, b) = 0. Both identities hold.

2. (Case s ≠ 0: factorisation.) Let L : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, L(z) := (−s)z. Since −s ≠ 0, L is a continuous linear equivalence (ContinuousLinearEquiv.smulLeft of the unit −s, with inverse z ↦ (−s)⁻¹z). Let T(w) := h(x + w). Then G = T ∘ L, because x − s z = x + (−s)z.

3. (Composition with an isomorphism needs no differentiability.)
- For any function F and continuous linear equivalence L, F ∘ L is differentiable at y iff F is differentiable at L(y), since F = (F ∘ L) ∘ L⁻¹. If so, D(F ∘ L)(y) = DF(L y) ∘ L by the chain rule; otherwise both sides are 0. So D(F ∘ L)(y) = DF(L y) ∘ L always (ContinuousLinearEquiv.comp_right_fderiv).
- The same argument, applied inductively to iterated derivatives, gives iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (F ∘ L) y = (iteratedFDeriv ℝ k F (L y)) composed with L in every argument, for every k (ContinuousLinearEquiv.iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_right with the set univ, rewritten by iteratedFDerivWithin_univ).
- Likewise the translation w ↦ x + w is a diffeomorphism, so DT(w) = Dh(x + w) and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 T w = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h (x + w) for all w and every h (fderiv_comp_add_left, iteratedFDeriv_comp_add_left).

4. (First derivative.) By steps 2 and 3, DG(y)a = DT(L y)(L a) = Dh(x + (−s)y)((−s)a). By linearity of Dh(x − s y) this equals −s·Dh(x − s y)a.

5. (Second derivative.) By steps 2 and 3, D²G(y)(a, b) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h (x + (−s)y) ![(−s)a, (−s)b]. A continuous multilinear map M in two variables satisfies M(c₁m₁, c₂m₂) = c₁c₂·M(m₁, m₂) (ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_smul_univ). So this equals (−s)(−s)·D²h(x − s y)(a, b) = s²·D²h(x − s y)(a, b). ∎

    have hL : ∀ z, L z = (-s) • z := fun z => rfl

fderiv and iteratedFDeriv commute with composition by a continuous linear equivalence and with translation, for arbitrary functions (no differentiability needed).

subproblems.title: Differentiation under the integral sign for M(σ) = ∫ h(x − σy) g(|y|²) dy
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝⁿ (= Euclid n) be open, and let h : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C¹ on U. Let x ∈ ℝⁿ, r > 0 and R ∈ ℝ with closedBall(x, R) ⊆ U, and let g : ℝ → ℝ be continuous with g(t) = 0 for all t ≥ r². For σ ∈ ℝ let M(σ) := ∫_{ℝⁿ} h(x − σy)·g(|y|²) dy. Then for every s ∈ ℝ with |s|·r < R, M is differentiable at s with M'(s) = −∫_{ℝⁿ} Dh(x − s y)(y)·g(|y|²) dy, where Dh(z) = fderiv ℝ h z.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (x : Euclid n) (r R : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U → closedBall x R ⊆ U → 0 < r → Continuous g → (∀ t : ℝ, r ^ 2 ≤ t → g t = 0) → ∀ s : ℝ, |s| * r < R → HasDerivAt (fun σ : ℝ => ∫ y : Euclid n, h (x - σ • y) * g (‖y‖ ^ 2)) (-∫ y : Euclid n, fderiv ℝ h (x - s • y) y * g (‖y‖ ^ 2)) s
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof, differentiation under the integral sign via hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le. The neighbourhood of s, the constants and all hypotheses are made explicit here.

Fix s with |s|r < R. Write F(σ, y) := h(x − σy)·g(|y|²) and F'(σ, y) := −(Dh(x − σy)(y)·g(|y|²)).

1. (A neighbourhood of s.) Let δ := (R − |s|r)/(2r) > 0 and R₁ := (|s| + δ)r = |s|r + (R − |s|r)/2 < R. Let J := (s − δ, s + δ), the ball of radius δ about s. For σ ∈ J, |σ| ≤ |s| + |σ − s| < |s| + δ, hence |σ|r < R₁ < R.

2. (Geometry.) |(x − σy) − x| = |σ||y|. Hence:
(a) if |σ|r < R and |y| ≤ r, then x − σy ∈ closedBall(x, R) ⊆ U;
(b) if σ ∈ J and |y| ≤ r, then |σ||y| ≤ (|s| + δ)r = R₁, i.e. x − σy ∈ closedBall(x, R₁).

3. (g beyond r.) If |y| ≥ r then |y|² ≥ r² (as r > 0), so g(|y|²) = 0. Hence F(σ, y) = 0 and F'(σ, y) = 0 for every σ.

4. (Constants.) U is open and h is C¹ on U. So h is continuous and differentiable at every point of U, and Dh is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
- closedBall(x, R₁) ⊆ closedBall(x, R) ⊆ U is compact, so ‖Dh‖ has a bound A₁ on closedBall(x, R₁) (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn).
- Let γ be a bound for |g| on the compact interval [0, r²]. Then |g(|y|²)| ≤ γ for all y: if |y| ≤ r then |y|² ∈ [0, r²]; otherwise g(|y|²) = 0 ≤ |g(0)| ≤ γ.

5. (Continuity in y.) Let σ satisfy |σ|r < R. Then y ↦ F(σ, y) is continuous on ℝⁿ:
- at y₀ with |y₀| ≤ r: x − σy₀ ∈ U by step 2(a), so h is continuous at x − σy₀. Since y ↦ x − σy is continuous, y ↦ h(x − σy) is continuous at y₀, and so is its product with the continuous map y ↦ g(|y|²);
- at y₀ with |y₀| > r: F(σ, ·) vanishes on the open set {|y| > r} ∋ y₀ by step 3.
The same argument, using continuity of Dh at x − s y₀ and of (L, y) ↦ L y, shows that y ↦ F'(s, y) is continuous. In particular F(σ, ·) for σ ∈ J and F'(s, ·) are a.e.-strongly measurable. Moreover F(s, ·) vanishes outside the compact set closedBall(0, r), so it is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).

6. (Pointwise derivative.) Let y ∈ ℝⁿ and σ ∈ J.
- If |y| < r: x − σy ∈ U by step 2(a) with step 1, so h is differentiable there. The map σ ↦ x − σy has derivative −y. By the chain rule, σ ↦ h(x − σy) has derivative Dh(x − σy)(−y) = −Dh(x − σy)(y). Multiplying by the constant g(|y|²) gives derivative F'(σ, y).
- If |y| ≥ r: σ ↦ F(σ, y) is identically 0 by step 3, with derivative 0 = F'(σ, y).

7. (Domination.) For σ ∈ J and every y, |F'(σ, y)| ≤ bound(y) := A₁·r·γ·1_{closedBall(0,r)}(y).
- If |y| ≤ r: |Dh(x − σy)(y)| ≤ ‖Dh(x − σy)‖·|y| ≤ A₁r, by step 2(b) and the choice of A₁; and |g(|y|²)| ≤ γ.
- If |y| > r: F'(σ, y) = 0.
The bound is integrable, being a constant times the indicator of closedBall(0, r), which has finite Lebesgue measure.

8. (Conclusion.) Apply hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le with the neighbourhood J of s; steps 5–7 supply its hypotheses. It gives that σ ↦ ∫ F(σ, y) dy = M(σ) has derivative ∫ F'(s, y) dy at s, and ∫ F'(s, y) dy = −∫ Dh(x − s y)(y)·g(|y|²) dy (integral_neg). ∎

subproblems.title: Vanishing of ∫ Dh(x − s y)(y) g(|y|²) dy for harmonic h and 0 < s ≤ 1
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝⁿ (= Euclid n) be open, and let h : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C² on U with Δh(y) := Σ_{i<n} D²h(y)(e_i, e_i) = 0 for all y ∈ U, where D²h(y)(a, b) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h y ![a, b] and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Let x ∈ ℝⁿ and 0 < r < R with closedBall(x, R) ⊆ U, let g : ℝ → ℝ be continuous with g(t) = 0 for all t ≥ r², and let 0 < s ≤ 1. Then ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dh(x − s y)(y)·g(|y|²) dy = 0, where Dh(z) = fderiv ℝ h z.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (h : Euclid n → ℝ), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 h U → (∀ y ∈ U, ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h y ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] = 0) → ∀ (x : Euclid n) (r R : ℝ), 0 < r → r < R → closedBall x R ⊆ U → ∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous g → (∀ t : ℝ, r ^ 2 ≤ t → g t = 0) → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ 1 → ∫ y : Euclid n, fderiv ℝ h (x - s • y) y * g (‖y‖ ^ 2) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (M'(s) = 0 for s ∈ (0, 1]). The radial potential, Green's identity and the scaling formulas come from the sibling lemmas radial_potential (Submission.dorag_ha_mv_radial_potential), green_identity (Submission.dorag_ha_mv_green_identity) and affine_comp_deriv (Submission.dorag_ha_mv_affine_comp_deriv).

1. (Radial potential.) By radial_potential applied to n, r, g, there is Ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ that is C¹, has compact support, satisfies tsupport Ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, r), and has DΨ(y)v = g(|y|²)⟨y, v⟩ for all y, v.

2. (The rescaled function.) Let V := ball(0, R), which is open, and G(z) := h(x − s z). For z ∈ V, |(x − s z) − x| = s|z| ≤ |z| < R because 0 < s ≤ 1, so x − s z ∈ closedBall(x, R) ⊆ U. The map z ↦ x − s z is affine, hence C^∞, and maps V into U. As h is C² on U, G is C² on V (ContDiffOn.comp).

3. (Support.) tsupport Ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, r) ⊆ ball(0, R) = V, because r < R (closedBall_subset_ball).

4. (Green.) green_identity applies to V, G, Ψ: V is open, G is C² on V, Ψ is C¹ with compact support, and tsupport Ψ ⊆ V. It gives
∫ Σ_i DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i dy = −∫ Ψ(y)·Σ_i D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) dy.

5. (The right side is 0.) Let y ∈ ℝⁿ.
- If y ∈ V: by affine_comp_deriv, D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) = s²·D²h(x − s y)(e_i, e_i) for each i. So Σ_i D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) = s²·Δh(x − s y) = 0, because x − s y ∈ U by step 2.
- If y ∉ V: then y ∉ tsupport Ψ by step 3, so Ψ(y) = 0.
In both cases Ψ(y)·Σ_i D²G(y)(e_i, e_i) = 0, so the right side of step 4 is −∫ 0 = 0.

6. (The left integrand.) Fix any y.
- By step 1, DΨ(y)e_i = g(|y|²)⟨y, e_i⟩.
- By affine_comp_deriv, which holds for every y and every function h, DG(y)e_i = −s·Dh(x − s y)e_i.
- y = Σ_i ⟨y, e_i⟩e_i (expansion in the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun; ⟨y, e_i⟩ = y_i). Since Dh(x − s y) is linear, Σ_i ⟨y, e_i⟩·Dh(x − s y)e_i = Dh(x − s y)(y).
Therefore
Σ_i DΨ(y)e_i·DG(y)e_i = Σ_i g(|y|²)⟨y, e_i⟩·(−s·Dh(x − s y)e_i) = −s·(Dh(x − s y)(y)·g(|y|²)).

7. (Conclusion.) By steps 4–6,
0 = ∫ −s·(Dh(x − s y)(y)·g(|y|²)) dy = −s·∫ Dh(x − s y)(y)·g(|y|²) dy.
Pulling a constant out of a Bochner integral needs no integrability (integral_const_mul). Since −s ≠ 0, ∫ Dh(x − s y)(y)·g(|y|²) dy = 0. ∎

theorem Submission.dorag_ha_mv_flux_zero : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid n)) (h : Euclid n → ℝ), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 h U → (∀ y ∈ U, ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h y ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] = 0) → ∀ (x : Euclid n) (r R : ℝ), 0 < r → r < R → closedBall x R ⊆ U → ∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous g → (∀ t : ℝ, r ^ 2 ≤ t → g t = 0) → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ 1 → ∫ y : Euclid n, fderiv ℝ h (x - s • y) y * g (‖y‖ ^ 2) = 0 := by

  obtain ⟨Ψ, hΨC, hΨc, hΨsupp, hΨd⟩ := Submission.dorag_ha_mv_radial_potential n r g hr hg hgr
  set G : Euclid n → ℝ := fun z => h (x - s • z) with hG
  have hVmaps : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : Euclid n) R, x - s • z ∈ U := by
    intro z hz
    apply hRU
    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, sub_sub_cancel_left, norm_neg, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_pos hs0]
    rw [mem_ball, dist_zero_right] at hz
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg z]
  have hGC : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 G (ball (0 : Euclid n) R) := by
    have hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 (fun z : Euclid n => x - s • z) := contDiff_const.sub (contDiff_id.const_smul s)
    exact hh.comp hA.contDiffOn (fun z hz => hVmaps z hz)
  have hsuppV : tsupport Ψ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) R := hΨsupp.trans (closedBall_subset_ball hrR)
  have hgreen := Submission.dorag_ha_mv_green_identity n (ball (0 : Euclid n) R) G Ψ isOpen_ball hGC hΨC hΨc hsuppV
  have hRHS : ∀ z, Ψ z * ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G z ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] = 0 := by
    intro z
    by_cases hz : z ∈ ball (0 : Euclid n) R
    · have hsum : ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 G z ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] = 0 := by
        simp_rw [hG, (Submission.dorag_ha_mv_affine_comp_deriv n h x s z _ _).2]
        rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hΔ _ (hVmaps z hz), mul_zero]
      rw [hsum, mul_zero]
    · have : Ψ z = 0 := image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport (fun h' => hz (hsuppV h'))
      rw [this, zero_mul]
  have hexp : ∀ (L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] ℝ) (z : Euclid n), ∑ i : Fin n, inner ℝ z (EuclideanSpace.single i (1:ℝ)) * L (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) = L z := by
    intro L z
    conv_rhs => rw [← (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).sum_repr z]
    rw [map_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    simp [EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right, map_smul]
  have hLHS : ∀ z, ∑ i : Fin n, fderiv ℝ Ψ z (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) * fderiv ℝ G z (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = -s * (fderiv ℝ h (x - s • z) z * g (‖z‖ ^ 2)) := by
    intro z
    have hGd : ∀ a, fderiv ℝ G z a = -(s * fderiv ℝ h (x - s • z) a) := fun a =>
      (Submission.dorag_ha_mv_affine_comp_deriv n h x s z a a).1
    simp_rw [hΨd, hGd]
    rw [← hexp (fderiv ℝ h (x - s • z)) z, Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_

  simp_rw [hLHS, hRHS, integral_zero, neg_zero, integral_const_mul] at hgreen

subproblems.title: Radial-kernel mean value identity implies the open-ball mean value identity
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, h : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), x ∈ ℝⁿ and r > 0, with h continuous on closedBall(x, r). Assume that for every continuous g : ℝ → ℝ with g(t) = 0 for all t ≥ r², ∫_{ℝⁿ} h(x − y)·g(|y|²) dy = h(x)·∫_{ℝⁿ} g(|y|²) dy. Then ∫_{B̆_r(x)} h = Lⁿ(B̆_r(x))·h(x). Here B̆_r(x) = ball(x, r) is the open ball, Lⁿ = volume is Lebesgue measure, and the measure is taken as a real number via ENNReal.toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (x : Euclid n) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ContinuousOn h (closedBall x r) → (∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous g → (∀ t : ℝ, r ^ 2 ≤ t → g t = 0) → ∫ y : Euclid n, h (x - y) * g (‖y‖ ^ 2) = h x * ∫ y : Euclid n, g (‖y‖ ^ 2)) → ∫ y in ball x r, h y = (volume (ball x r)).toReal * h x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (piecewise-linear profiles g_k → 1_{[0, r²)}, dominated convergence, and the reflection y ↦ x − y), with details.

1. (Profiles.) For k ∈ ℕ let g_k(t) := min{1, max{0, (k + 1)(r² − t)}}. Each g_k is continuous and 0 ≤ g_k ≤ 1. If t ≥ r² then (k + 1)(r² − t) ≤ 0, so g_k(t) = min{1, 0} = 0. In particular g_k(|y|²) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ r.

2. (Pointwise limit.) For every y, g_k(|y|²) → 1_{ball(0,r)}(y) as k → ∞.
- If |y| < r, then c := r² − |y|² > 0. Choose K ∈ ℕ with K ≥ 1/c. For k ≥ K, (k + 1)c ≥ 1, so g_k(|y|²) = 1.
- If |y| ≥ r, then g_k(|y|²) = 0 for all k, by step 1.

3. (Bounds.) closedBall(x, r) is compact and h is continuous on it, so there is A₀ with |h(z)| ≤ A₀ for all z ∈ closedBall(x, r).
- If |y| ≤ r, then x − y ∈ closedBall(x, r), so |h(x − y)·g_k(|y|²)| ≤ A₀.
- If |y| > r, the product is 0.
Hence |h(x − y)·g_k(|y|²)| ≤ A₀·1_{closedBall(0,r)}(y) and |g_k(|y|²)| ≤ 1_{closedBall(0,r)}(y). Both bounds are integrable: constants times the indicator of a set of finite measure.

4. (Measurability.) y ↦ g_k(|y|²) is continuous. The function y ↦ h(x − y)·g_k(|y|²) vanishes for |y| > r, so it equals its own product with 1_{closedBall(0,r)}. On the closed, hence measurable, set closedBall(0, r) it is continuous, because y ↦ x − y maps closedBall(0, r) into closedBall(x, r), where h is continuous. So it is a.e.-strongly measurable (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable together with aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff).

5. (Dominated convergence.) By tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence and steps 2–4,
a_k := ∫ h(x − y)·g_k(|y|²) dy → ∫ h(x − y)·1_{ball(0,r)}(y) dy, and
b_k := ∫ g_k(|y|²) dy → ∫ 1_{ball(0,r)}(y) dy.

6. (Use the hypothesis.) Each g_k is continuous and vanishes on [r², ∞) (step 1), so the hypothesis gives a_k = h(x)·b_k for all k. Hence a_k → h(x)·∫ 1_{ball(0,r)}, and by uniqueness of limits
∫ h(x − y)·1_{ball(0,r)}(y) dy = h(x)·∫ 1_{ball(0,r)}(y) dy.

7. (Left side.) h(x − y)·1_{ball(0,r)}(y) = 1_{ball(0,r)}(y)·h(x − y), so the left side is ∫_{ball(0,r)} h(x − y) dy (integral_indicator). The map φ(y) := x − y preserves Lebesgue measure (Measure.measurePreserving_sub_left) and is a measurable embedding, being a measurable equivalence. Also φ⁻¹(ball(x, r)) = ball(0, r), since |(x − y) − x| = |y|. Hence
∫_{ball(0,r)} h(x − y) dy = ∫_{φ⁻¹(ball(x,r))} h(φ(y)) dy = ∫_{ball(x,r)} h(z) dz (MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb).

8. (Right side.) ∫ 1_{ball(0,r)} = Lⁿ(ball(0, r)) as a real number (integral_indicator_one). By translation invariance (Measure.addHaar_ball_center), Lⁿ(ball(0, r)) = Lⁿ(ball(x, r)), which is finite; its real value is (volume(ball(x, r))).toReal.

9. Combining steps 6–8: ∫_{ball(x,r)} h = h(x)·(volume(ball(x, r))).toReal = (volume(ball(x, r))).toReal·h(x). ∎

    have : ((k : ℝ) + 1) * (r ^ 2 - t) ≤ 0 :=

    · push Not at hy
      rw [indicator_of_notMem (by rwa [mem_ball, dist_zero_right, not_lt])]

    intro y hy; rw [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, sub_sub_cancel_left, norm_neg]; exact hy
  have hcb : ∀ y : Euclid n, y ∈ closedBall (0 : Euclid n) r ↔ ‖y‖ ≤ r := fun y => by

      by_cases hy : ‖y‖ ≤ r

    refine ContinuousOn.mul ?_ ((gk_cont k).comp (by fun_prop : Continuous fun y : Euclid n => ‖y‖ ^ 2)).continuousOn
